sections.title: Who proved that the earth is spherical?
sections.description: Use the original spherical Earth figure plus distinct animated beats of a ship disappearing over the horizon, curved Earth shadow at lunar eclipse, and a circumnavigation route; labels remain authored, not AI-generated.
sections.narration_script: Who proved that the earth is spherical? Many ancient civilizations believed that the Earth was flat. However, Greek philosopher Pythagoras was one of the first to suggest that the Earth is spherical. Later, Aristotle provided evidence by observing how ships disappear over the horizon and how the Earth's shadow on the Moon is curved during a lunar eclipse. Ferdinand Magellan's voyage around the world further confirmed that the Earth is round.

sections.title: Rotation
sections.description: Animate west-to-east Earth spin and the advancing day-night boundary; insert the exact textbook axial-tilt figure with legible original equator, axis and 23.45-degree diagram labels while the body text's 23.5-degree value is read.
sections.narration_script: Rotation. Rotation is the movement of the Earth around its own axis is called Rotation. The earth rotates from west to east. It completes one full rotation in 24 hours. The speed of rotation is faster at the equator and slower at the poles. The axis is tilted at an angle of 23.5°. As the Earth is spherical in shape, only one half of the Earth receives sunlight at a time. Thus, the side of the Earth facing the Sun experience day. On the other hand, the other half, or the part away from the sun, experiences night. As the Earth rotates, the lighted part moves into the darkness. Rotation causes day and night.

sections.title: Revolution
sections.description: Show a continuous 3D tilted Earth orbit around the Sun with changing daylight; use the exact rotation-versus-revolution textbook figure and distinct summer, winter, spring and autumn visual beats when each season is spoken.
sections.narration_script: Revolution. Revolution is the movement of the Earth around the Sun in a fixed path called an orbit. The Earth revolves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit. It takes 365¼ days (one year) to complete one revolution. The tilt of the Earth's axis remains the same during revolution. Revolution causes seasonal changes. The revolution of the Earth and the tilt of its axis cause different seasons: Summer – The hemisphere tilted towards the Sun experiences summer. Winter – The hemisphere tilted away from the Sun experiences winter. Spring – Occurs between winter and summer when the temperature starts rising. Autumn – Occurs between summer and winter when the temperature starts dropping.

sections.title: What is Solstice and When Does It Occur?
sections.description: Show the tilted Earth and Sun at December and June positions; keep December 22, June 21, Tropic of Capricorn and Tropic of Cancer as precise authored labels synchronized to the narration.
sections.narration_script: What is Solstice and When Does It Occur? A solstice is a day, when the sun shines vertically over a Tropic (both cancer and Capricorn) in the afternoon and the day is the longest in that hemisphere. On 22 December, the rays of the sun fall directly over the Tropic of Capricorn. This is the longest day in Southern Hemisphere (summer season), while in the Northern Hemisphere, it is the shortest day (winter season). This is called 'Winter Solstice. On 21 June, sunlight falls vertically over the Tropic of Cancer. This is the longest day in Northern Hemisphere and hence it is called 'Summer Solstice', while in the Southern Hemisphere, it is the shortest day.

sections.description: Show equal illuminated and dark Earth halves, then the complete original four-position solstice/equinox source diagram; keep all four date captions readable and correctly placed.
sections.narration_script: What is Equinox and When Does It Occur? The sun falls directly on the equator two times in a year. During this period there is equal length of day and night all over the world. In Northern Hemisphere, the March Equinox is called the Vernal or Spring Equinox while September Equinox is called Autumnal Equinox. Spring Equinox (March 21st) marks the beginning of spring. Autumn Equinox (September 23rd) marks the beginning of autumn.

sections.narration_script: Let's Remember. The Earth moves in two ways: rotation and revolution. Rotation causes day and night, while revolution causes seasons. The Earth completes one rotation in 24 hours and one revolution in 365¼ days. Solstices occur in June and December, marking the longest and shortest days. Equinoxes occur in March and September, when day and night are equal.
